chen: quick heads-up — ran the new perf sweep on the mixed-GPU pool (A10 + T4 respins). seeing a consistent ~9-12% slower tail for seq=512 when our autotuner picks the small-kernel fastpath
chen: interestingly the median is fine, tail is what spikes, looks like a misrouted kernel for some hw signatures
jess: can you paste the perf_trace and the kernel name it picked?
chen: attaching snippet from the probe run:
```
probe: device=GPU_A10_2 model=ga102-sm86 flags=hw_sig:0x3a
selected_kernel: fast_dot_accel_v2 (seqlen<=128 optimized)
fallback: generic_matmul_v1 (used for >128)
observed_path: fast_dot_accel_v2 used at seq=512, then fallback to generic_matmul_v1 mid-run
latency_p95: 210ms -> 235ms when switching path
```
chen: seems like our detection logic classified this A10 as compatible with the tiny-tile kernel, but its tensor core config causes throughput cliff at long sequences
dmitri: that's wild — could be the capflag mask we compute from driver query. we added an aggressive compatibility heuristic last month to prefer fast_dot on any device advertising fp16 tensor cores
emma: that heuristic was intended to lower median, but it didn't consider cache-pressure for kv-cache at longer sequences. when KV cache eviction happens the tiny-tile path thrashes L2 leading to mid-run fallback and extra syncs
jess: do we have a repro script? try `./autotune-replay --device GPU_A10_2 --seqlen 512 --batch 1 --trace-kernels` and collect kernel timestamps
chen: ran that. trace shows the kernel switch at token 130 in the generation; also the kernel launch time variance jumps right before switch
chen: here's a summarized flame (very condensed):
```
fast_dot_accel_v2: spikes @ tokens 120-140 (gpu stalls)
generic_matmul_v1: steady but higher baseline; no stalls
```
jess: hypothesis: our feature-detect reports tensor-core fp16 but not the per-SM maximum warp-size alignment needed by fast_dot_accel_v2. kernel assumes `warp_tiles % 4 == 0` and misaligns on some A10 firmware combos
dmitri: i can add an extra gate in the probe where we sanity-check kernel microbench results (latency on seqlen=256 and seqlen=512) before enabling the tiny-tile path. cheap microbench run (<1s) at startup
emma: also consider a KV-cache-aware cost model in autotuner: incorporate estimated eviction rate into kernel selection score. if eviction_rate > 0.1 prefer generic kernel
chen: for quick mitigation we can set a per-hw override flag to disable fast_dot_accel_v2 for devices matching driver=510.* and hw_sig range 0x30-0x3f. will push a candidate to staging
jess: please add an integration test that runs seq=512 with kv-cache enabled and asserts no mid-run kernel switches for 50 runs
dmitri: working on both: probe gate + integration. also will add logging to the compile-time kernel pick so we can audit decisions in console
infra-bot: deploy/edge-autotune-2026-03 rolled out to staging at 3789012380 :white_check_mark:
emma: once staging passes, we should backfill a quick perf sweep across all regions to catch other firmware combos. I'll schedule a 2hr sweep window tonight
chen: ok, I'll open a tiny RFC with the workaround + longer-term autotuner changes (kv-aware scoring + microbench gate). tagging @jess @dmitri for review :thumbsup:
jess: thanks — low risk fix. if staging looks good we can hotfix prod reserves for Dedicated nodes this afternoon
chen: updated PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/5423 — includes probe gate + hw blacklist config
dmitri: will add the microbench harness in a follow-up PR, tests included
emma: great team work, feel free to escalate if we still see tail after the rollout
